html:
The 1981 protests in Kosovo began on 11 March 1981 with students at the University of Pristina complaining about food, and grew into mass demonstrations demanding that Kosovo become a full republic of Yugoslavia.

Kosovo was then an autonomous province of Serbia, with an Albanian majority and the lowest income in the country. The army and police put the protests down; the official count was a few dozen dead, and thousands were jailed. The crackdown hardened Albanian demands, while Serbs spoke of being pushed out. Within a few years Slobodan Milošević rose on Serb anger over Kosovo and in 1989 stripped the province of its autonomy, a step toward the breakup of Yugoslavia.
sum: The 1981 protests in Kosovo began on 11 March 1981 with students at the University of Pristina complaining about food, and grew into mass demonstrations demanding that Kosovo become a full republic of Yugoslavia.
